title: Is extracting the notification service ready to start?

masthead.headline: The direction is settled. This board is only about whether to start now.
masthead.lede: Nothing here argues for or against extracting notifications. It measures the six things the extraction would need and reports which of them exist today.

sections.label: Verdict
sections.title: Four of six ready; the two that are not are the expensive ones.

points.text: The send path is already behind an interface, the queue exists, and templates were moved out of the monolith in July. None of that is the problem.
Three teams send notifications and none is willing to be paged for delivery failures. An extraction that lands without an owner produces a service that decays.
Six callers use the interface and only its happy path is covered, so the extraction would be a rewrite with no way to tell whether behaviour changed.

items.label: Interface stability
items.note: Unchanged for four months across six callers.

items.label: Test coverage of the seam
items.note: Happy path only. No test asserts what happens when a provider rejects.

items.label: Operational ownership
items.note: No team has accepted the pager. This is the gap that blocks a start date.

items.label: Data separation
items.note: One remaining join against the user table, in the digest builder.

items.label: Deploy independence
items.note: Pipeline exists; the shared config package still forces a lockstep release.

items.label: Rollback path
items.note: Reversible by flag for the first two weeks, then not.

cells.text: Twelve tests touch the port; all twelve assert a successful send.
Asked all three sending teams in the 19 Aug platform sync. None accepted.

text: is a compile-time dependency of both sides.

cells.text: The flag works until the first schema divergence, which the plan puts in week three.

blocks.title: Two readings are the author's judgement, not a measurement
blocks.text: Neither has been tried. They are marked assumed and estimated rather than dressed as findings, and either could move a point in each direction once someone attempts it.

sections.label: The gaps
sections.title: What has to be true before this starts.

items.title: Name the owning team
items.text: One team accepts the pager for delivery failures and the on-call rotation absorbs it. Without this the rest is wasted motion.

items.title: Write the contract tests against the current implementation
items.text: Six callers, every failure mode the providers actually return. These are written before extraction so they describe today's behaviour rather than the new service's.

items.title: Break the shared config dependency
items.text: Already scoped; two days, no design decisions left in it.

items.title: Remove the digest builder's join against the user table
items.text: Replaced by the identity read model, which shipped in July.

blocks.label: Accepted blockers
blocks.ask: Which of these do you agree must be closed before the extraction starts, rather than during it?

options.summary: No extraction begins until one team has accepted the pager.
Written against the current implementation, before any code moves.
The shared config dependency is broken first rather than carried.

options.value: A rollback that survives week three
options.summary: Either the schema divergence moves later or the flag is replaced by something durable.

blocks.label: Start confidence
blocks.ask: If the two blocking gaps were closed tomorrow, how confident would you be starting the week after?

points.label: 2 — Only with a smaller first slice

sources.label: Rollback durability past week three
